blocker.summary: The r399 allocator double-issue is RESOLVED (r413/r414/r415: r366's own invented critical-section fix in sub_821FA9E0 clobbered its own return value, silently discarding every C++ static-initializer array growth and causing an unbounded heap overflow; fixed and live-verified, r398's exact original repro no longer double-issues). r416/r417 established boot now progresses past sub_821D5F48 and the per-frame loop (sub_821D7DE0, unconditionally infinite, no bug) runs sustained at a realistic ~16-17ms cadence; the 'generated entry terminated its own thread' message is r277's designed clean-shutdown behavior firing when the probe window elapses, not a stall. So there is no known blocker in the allocator chain, boot sequence, or per-frame loop's own execution. r418 answered the presented_frames=0 question cheaply (a host-side grep, before spending budget reading guest PPC as r417 had named): diagnostics_.presented_frames is written ONLY by NativeRuntime::submit_ring(), whose only caller anywhere in the tree is native/tests/native_runtime_tests.cpp -- this was already found by a PRE-r399 cycle, r292 (artifacts/retail-us-native-r292-gpu-drain-check/), confirmed independently again this cycle. It is dead-code wiring, unrelated to r399-r417. The REAL GPU path (NativeGuestVdService, native/src/native_guest_vd.cpp, also identified by r292) was re-probed with AC6_NATIVE_VD_TRACE=1 on the r414-fixed binary: r293 had found this ring goes silent after one short burst ('the guest has stopped publishing', not a host bug); on the fixed binary it does NOT go silent anymore -- 11 accepted drain batches over 25s (vs r294's original 5), write_index climbing continuously (25->43->49->55->67->73) -- a real, measurable improvement plausibly downstream of r414's fix, though not proven by a controlled A/B in this cycle. But every single drain batch still shows present=0 -- no Present packet is ever emitted by the guest in the observed window, so presented_frames would stay 0 even with the dead-code wiring fixed. A NEW, separate symptom was also observed and is NOT yet characterized: with AC6_NATIVE_VD_TRACE=1, the process took roughly 100-150s beyond its configured 25s probe window to exit (a `timeout 40` did not stop it; it had to be killed) -- this was NOT seen on the plain r414-r417 runs (clean exit within seconds of window elapse), but no controlled A/B isolating the trace flag as the actual cause was run this cycle. Named for r419, in order: (1) isolate whether the slow-exit symptom is specific to AC6_NATIVE_VD_TRACE=1 before calling it a real blocker; (2) if confirmed independent of the trace flag, read sub_821D7AE0/sub_821D7CD0 (never read yet) to find where a Present packet would be emitted and why it isn't. The standing uncommitted-tree situation (r239+, over the 2026-09-02 mass deletion) remains the user's decision, untouched -- reports and named tool scripts for r413-r418 were committed individually, the broader tree state was not.
